findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify HOW the `supports_temperature` override identifies only the affected Bedrock models when `BedrockModelProfile` carries no per-model identifier: either (a) extend `ModelCapabilities`/`capabilities_for` to accept a model-string argument that predicates can match against, (b) introduce a separate `_TEMPERATURE_UNSUPPORTED_MODELS: frozenset[str]` lookup (keyed by model string, consulted alongside the profile path), or (c) explicitly acknowledge in the plan that `supports_temperature=False` is applied to ALL Bedrock-hosted Anthropic models and document the determinism tradeoff.
evidence: Plan: 'add a rebar override entry that withdraws it for the affected Bedrock models; `runner.py` omits `temperature` from `model_settings` when the capability is False'
Existing `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` schema (capabilities.py:68-70): predicates receive only a `ModelProfile` object and read profile TYPE + profile FIELDS — no model-name/ID field is present.

Plan: 'Rejected alternatives: dropping temperature on ALL Bedrock calls (loses the greedy Pass-2 determinism that keeps verification stable)' — yet that is the only predicate expressible with the current profile-only table.
capabilities.py:50-52: both arms of `_is_claude` read isinstance and getattr on the profile — no model-name channel exists in the predicate signature.

Measured evidence names `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` as the fatal model, while `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` (the documented default) works fine — distinguishing them requires a model-ID lookup, not a profile-field predicate.
findings.finding: The `supports_temperature` capability override cannot target specific Bedrock model IDs using the current profile-predicate table: `BedrockModelProfile` does not carry a per-model identifier field that predicates can read, so a predicate cannot distinguish `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (temperature fatal) from `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` (temperature fine). Setting `supports_temperature=False` for all Bedrock Claude models (the only expressible predicate) would strip temperature from sonnet-4-6 too, breaking the greedy Pass-2 determinism the plan specifically calls out as a motivation for keeping temperature on working models.
findings.location: Approach / Decision C — 'Add `supports_temperature: bool` to `ModelCapabilities` … add a rebar override entry that withdraws it for the affected Bedrock models'
scenarios: If the predicate matches all Bedrock-hosted Anthropic models, temperature is omitted for claude-sonnet-4-6 too, breaking Pass-2 greedy verification on the recommended default.
If the predicate is narrowed to not match claude-sonnet-4-6, the override table's schema must be extended (e.g. to accept model-string matchers), which is an undocumented design change.

If implemented as a hard-coded model-string set in runner.py instead of the capability table, it violates the plan's stated rationale ('keeps the decision in the single capability registry instead of a provider-name branch').
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `_BEDROCK_TEMPERATURE_UNSUPPORTED: frozenset[str]` set in `capabilities.py` (or `bedrock_model.py`) listing confirmed-fatal model IDs (initially `{'us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7', 'global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7'}`). In `capabilities_for`, when the model is a string, check it against this set and set `supports_temperature=False` directly — bypassing the profile-predicate path for this one capability. This keeps the decision in the capability module (not runner.py), handles model-ID-level precision, and is extensible as more models are measured.

findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope section for `capabilities.py`, add: 'The sidecar reader (story 343b) MUST be configured with `extra="ignore"` (or equivalent) before this field is written, so old and new readers can coexist. On rollback, sidecars already written with `supports_temperature` remain readable by old code. If the sidecar is cryptographically signed over the full payload, the signing scope must exclude unknown-future fields, or the signature scheme must be versioned.'
